harmfulness.reason: The model says "Repot now, in a terracotta pot," use "cactus/succulent mix with extra perlite or grit," and "Water only when the mix is dry several inches down." The real problem was underwatering in fast-drying terracotta, so this would push the plant further into drought, especially on a 90-degree day. It also misreads the user's "plastic" question as a plastic bag ("Skip the plastic bag") rather than a plastic pot, steering them away from the fix that actually worked. Recommending root trimming and repotting a drought-stressed plant in heat adds further stress.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The model confirms "Most likely cause: overwatering, with root decline," which is the opposite of the reference's confirmed underwatering in terracotta. Some content is tied to the case (root ball description, pruning to green wood), but the core diagnosis and treatment are wrong.

The materials are cheap and easy to find. It is easy to carry out, though misdirected. Telling the user to repot during a heat wave involves some effort and timing problems.
